views.description: ArchiMate-inspired motivation viewpoint for framing stakeholder concerns before modeling solution details. Stakeholders: business partners, business managers, requirements owners, enterprise architects, and acceptors. Concerns: architecture mission, drivers for change, assessments, high-level goals, desired outcomes, value, principles, and hard constraints. Purpose: designing, deciding, and informing. Scope: motivation and strategy context. Use this view to answer who cares, why the change matters, what success means, and which constraints cannot be violated. Typical elements: Stakeholder, Driver, Assessment, Goal, Outcome, Value, Meaning, Principle, Requirement, Constraint, Course of Action. Do not place implementation components here unless they are needed only as evidence for a stakeholder concern.

ArchiMate-inspired strategy viewpoint combining Strategy, Capability Map, Value Stream, and Outcome Realization concerns. Stakeholders: business managers, product owners, enterprise architects, business architects, and portfolio decision-makers. Concerns: business-oriented results, capability boundaries, value streams, resources, investment focus, and capability-to-outcome coverage. Purpose: designing and deciding. Scope: strategy with links to motivation and core elements when needed. Use this view to answer what business outcomes are in scope, which capabilities create or support them, and where value is produced. Typical elements: Outcome, Capability, Value Stream, Resource, Course of Action, Product, Value, Meaning, and selectively core elements that realize outcomes. Do not decompose detailed workflows or technical implementation here.

ArchiMate-inspired business behavior viewpoint drawing from Organization, Product, and Business Process Cooperation viewpoints. Stakeholders: process owners, domain experts, operational managers, business analysts, and product managers. Concerns: responsibilities, authority, business process dependencies, business services, product composition, contracts, shared information, and observable business events. Purpose: designing, deciding, and informing. Scope: mainly Business layer, with application links only when they explain business process support. Use this view to answer how the business works, who performs behavior, what events trigger it, what business objects are used, and what services or products are exposed. Typical elements: Business Actor, Business Role, Business Collaboration, Business Process, Business Function, Business Interaction, Business Event, Business Service, Business Object, Contract, Product, Representation. Do not turn this view into an application structure or code module map.

ArchiMate-inspired realization and usage viewpoint combining Requirements Realization, Application Usage, Service Realization, Application Cooperation, and Implementation and Deployment concerns. Stakeholders: enterprise architects, application architects, solution architects, process architects, and implementation designers. Concerns: how requirements, capabilities, business processes, and business services are realized by application services, components, data objects, and supporting technology; consistency, completeness, dependency visibility, and service orchestration. Purpose: designing and deciding. Scope: multiple layers and multiple aspects, but only along business-to-system realization paths. Use this view to answer how a business capability is carried by system responsibilities and which application or technology elements are relevant to that realization. Typical elements: Requirement, Constraint, Capability, Business Service, Business Process, Application Service, Application Component, Application Interface, Application Function or Process, Data Object, Technology Service, Node, Artifact. Do not include low-level implementation detail unless it changes a business-visible responsibility or dependency.

ArchiMate-inspired implementation and migration viewpoint extended with ARGO acceptance semantics. Stakeholders: business acceptors, project managers, operational managers, enterprise architects, delivery owners, and downstream agents. Concerns: acceptance control points, observation points, risk, work package scope, deliverables, plateaus, gaps, migration order, cross-cutting concerns, and consistency between delivery dependencies and architecture dependencies. Purpose: deciding and informing, with enough design detail to plan delivery. Scope: implementation and migration plus explicit business acceptance semantics. Use this view to answer how the change will be accepted, what must be observed, which work packages or plateaus are involved, what depends on what, and what risks could invalidate delivery. Typical elements: Goal, Outcome, Requirement, Constraint, Work Package, Deliverable, Implementation Event, Plateau, Gap, Business Actor, Business Role, and core elements affected by delivery. Do not use this view as a backlog dump; every item must affect acceptance, sequencing, or risk.

Top-level baseline architecture map governed by five universal business viewpoints. It follows the ArchiMate viewpoint mechanism: select content by stakeholder concerns, purpose, and scope, not by layer folders. The five child viewpoints provide the default AI navigation path from stakeholder intent to outcomes and capabilities, business behavior, capability realization, and acceptance-delivery sequencing. ArchiMate layers remain implicit in element types and may be used by validators or specialized sub-views, but they are not the default modeling entry point.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: downstream Agents retain complete no-argument reading while optionally consuming coherent semantic query results; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: compatibility, consumer behavior, canonical source, and observable outcome; Rationale: this view shows how the intent-query application service supports the business consumption process without removing the full-snapshot behavior.

views.view_name: Graph RAG Request and Purpose Usage
views.description: Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: query mode and purpose are explicit, reproducible, and version-safe; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: request semantics, mode validation, purpose selection, and semantic availability; Rationale: this view expresses the application behavior that interprets Agent requests before retrieval and closure.

views.view_name: Graph RAG Seed and Closure Usage
views.description: Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: ordinary semantic retrieval separates relevance selection from minimal deterministic structural closure while keeping returned content canonical; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: independent seed channels, deterministic purpose expansion, relationship endpoint closure, complete non-cascading View closure, canonical graph authority, and provenance; Rationale: this view is an Application Usage Viewpoint instance because it shows the application behavior dependency chain from semantic selection to required endpoint/View completion, with canonical object authority and without similarity-driven neighbor expansion.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: each lifecycle task obtains a bounded, reproducible, and independently reviewable closure policy; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: purpose-policy dispatch and the five accepted lifecycle purposes, with each category selected by declared purpose and parameterized policy rather than Agent identity or generated Cypher; Rationale: this view shows the distinct application behaviors selected by the declared task purpose and the Triggering relationships that keep category boundaries independent.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: purpose-specific results converge on common structural integrity rules without erasing independent purpose-category boundaries; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: five lifecycle policies, relationship endpoints, and complete Views; Rationale: this companion view preserves shared post-closure integrity obligations while keeping W5 category selection separate from W6 endpoint/View integrity and within the repository View element limit.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: every returned relationship and matched View is structurally coherent, every returned object has explainable inclusion provenance, and the coherent result is blocked if canonical-version evidence is missing; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: W6 endpoint closure, complete non-cascading View closure, single first-inclusion provenance, DT-00 coherent-version regression, canonical authority, and coherent outcome; Rationale: this view instantiates the Application Usage Viewpoint because it shows how query-service application behavior turns W5 selected ranges into consumer-readable context with traceable version evidence, without adding W7 quality scoring or capacity decisions.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: semantic retrieval never contradicts the canonical graph version and Phase 1 correctness is proven by exact threshold-all behavior before ANN comparison; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: all-mutation index lifecycle, semantic-index version evidence, threshold-all seed correctness, alignment states, stale-query rejection, and canonical read continuity; Rationale: this view models the application and data dependencies governing semantic-query availability while making ANN top-k benchmark-only and preserving canonical reads when the index is not Aligned.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: upstream version and request prerequisites are visible in their business dependency order; Purpose: handoff preparation; Scope: canonical mutation through purpose-policy selection; Rationale: this view instantiates the first half of the accepted vertical dependency chain and makes prerequisite direction explicit.

views.view_name: Graph RAG Quality and Capacity Acceptance
views.description: Viewpoint: Implementation and Migration Viewpoint; Concern: phase-1 retrieval is accepted only through approved business benchmark evidence while undecided capacity controls remain explicit; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: W7 quality gate, DT-00 coherent outcome context, observed precision and cardinality, and deferred phase-2 capacity governance; Rationale: this view belongs under the acceptance-delivery anchor because it defines the business release evidence proving recall and closure before whole delivery while keeping DT-19 capacity choices out of Phase 1 correctness.

Viewpoint: Implementation and Migration Viewpoint; Concern: closure, provenance, quality proof, and deferred capacity decisions occur in an explicit delivery sequence; Purpose: handoff preparation; Scope: purpose expansion through phase-2 decision evidence; Rationale: this view instantiates the acceptance-facing half of the vertical dependency chain without mixing it with request or index design concerns.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: graph-tidy and omitted-query consumers continue to receive exact canonical full snapshots and are not treated as debug/evidence response modes; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: graph-tidy purpose selection, query service full-read compatibility, canonical graph authority, and complete snapshot access; Rationale: this view is an Application Usage Viewpoint instance because it isolates the graph-tidy application usage path from ordinary semantic subset retrieval while preserving canonical authority and public compatibility.

Viewpoint: Technology Usage Viewpoint; Concern: production runtime, canonical authority, independent embedding generation, native semantic retrieval, and Neo4j vector-projection dependencies; Purpose: designing and deciding; Scope: query service through Node.js adapter and Neo4j-native seed/index technology; Rationale: this view shows the production application-to-technology path while keeping canonical JSON authoritative and excluding Python or GenAI Plugin as required dependencies.

Viewpoint: Technology Usage Viewpoint; Concern: provider/model qualification, secure credentials, production adapter coupling, and vector persistence before index delivery; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: runtime, native retrieval, open qualification gate, credentials, provider-neutral service, independent adapter, and semantic index; Rationale: this view separates the qualified production provider path from optional Neo4j GenAI Plugin qualification/backfill/benchmark use.

Viewpoint: Application Usage Viewpoint; Concern: Agent-facing ARGO MCP architecture reads expose only canonical full snapshots or structurally closed canonical subsets through the public getSystemArchitecture usage path; Purpose: deciding and handoff preparation; Scope: consumer, process, MCP interface, query service, request data, validation, and observable coherent context; Rationale: this view is an Application Usage Viewpoint instance because it shows how the Agent-facing application interface and query service support business intent-context consumption while request validation constrains the public response contract.
